title: 120-year-old church bell weighing 300 pounds stolen from belfry in rural Manitoba
summary: The case of the stolen church bell has police sounding an alarm — and scratching their heads.

image.caption: The bell stolen from the Sacred Heart of Jesus church is estimated to weigh more than 130 kilograms. RCMP don't know how or when the bell was removed from the tower. (Submitted by RCMP)

blocks.text: Manitoba
The case of the stolen church bell has police sounding an alarm — and scratching their heads.
Damage seen at top of belfry but RCMP unsure how heavy bell removed

A bell estimated to weigh 300 pounds (about 136 kilograms) was somehow removed from a wooden belfry at the Sacred Heart of Jesus Ukrainian Catholic Church, about 80 kilometres north of Winnipeg near Fraserwood, Man.
RCMP don't know how or when it was removed.
"It's still a bit of a mystery," RCMP Const. Merry Ploeg told CBC Monday, adding the bell is unique.
"It's brass, [and] it's got some ornate designs, including a rosary," she said, adding it also has an image of the sacred heart surrounded by a crown of thorns, crucifix and an anchor.
"We would really appreciate the public being kind of aware of it and on the lookout."
The theft was reported Saturday, RCMP said in a Monday news release.
Rev. Andriy Rabiy, auxiliary bishop of the Archeparchy of Winnipeg — which oversees Ukrainian Catholic churches in Manitoba — said he felt "great disbelief and shock" when he heard what happened.
"Sometimes we hear about break-ins into those kind of abandoned churches … [with] some small things being taken," he said.
"But not to that degree."
Rabiy said Sacred Heart of Jesus is one of two Ukrainian Catholic parishes in the Fraserwood area, with a history that goes back to when the first Ukrainians arrived in Manitoba.
Damage can be seen at the top of the wooden belfry. (Submitted by RCMP)
The number of parishioners has dwindled as people have left farming communities, he said, and the church is now mainly used for special occasions like funerals or annual liturgy services.
But those who remain in the community care deeply about the building, said Rabiy.
"Many of those churches actually kind of … stand as a witness to the past history that they had," Rabiy said.
"I can only imagine what kind of ache, of pain people experience," he said, adding that there is at least one person offering a $500 reward for any information that could help get the bell back.
Scrap dealers notified to watch for bell: RCMP
The wood-clad belfry is about 1½ storeys tall and stands on its own at the back of the church in Manitoba's Interlake region, about 12 kilometres northwest of Gimli.
The RCMP officers who investigated the theft found noticeable damage to the top of the belfry, police said in Monday's news release.
Ploeg didn't want to speculate on why someone would take the bell, but said the only thing RCMP can think of is that someone might try selling it for scrap metal.
"We've actually contacted all the scrap metal and recycling businesses in the area, including in Winnipeg, and notified them to be on the lookout for this bell specifically," Ploeg said.

The Manitoba Historical Society says the belfry was imported from Switzerland when the original church was built in 1906. That church was destroyed by fire in 1940, and the present church was built in 1942.
The bell is also from Switzerland and came at the same time, RCMP said.
The small church is a mission of the much larger Church of the Sacred Heart of Jesus in Gimli.

items: Church bell and memorial plaques stolen from oldest surviving Ukrainian Catholic Church in Canada

blocks.text: Ploeg said the parishioners are extremely concerned, as is she, by the fact someone went to such lengths to take the bell.
"Should the other churches be maybe … [be] looking at getting security footage or more regularly checking their properties?" she said.
"Everybody involved is very invested in seeing the bell returned. I'm really hoping that we can get it back and that it isn't scrap."
RCMP are asking anyone who has any information about the theft or noticed anything suspicious in the area over the last week to contact them at 204-642-5106.
